target_concept: Describe how a hash set is used to detect whether a character is common to all strings at a given position.

mcq.questionText: When using a hash set to determine whether the characters at a specific index are common to all strings, which of the following describes the correct procedure?
options: Add the character from each string at that index to a hash set; if after processing all strings the set size is 1, the character is common to all strings at that position.
Add each character to a list and count how many times it appears; if the count equals the number of strings, the character is common.
Store the indices of strings containing the character in a hash set; if the set contains all string indices, the character is common.
If the hash set contains more than one element, it indicates that the character appears in all strings.
mcq.correctAnswer: Add the character from each string at that index to a hash set; if after processing all strings the set size is 1, the character is common to all strings at that position.
mcq.explanation: A hash set eliminates duplicates, so adding the character from each string at the same position will result in a set size of one only when every string has the identical character at that position. Any differing character will increase the set size beyond one.
